title: Poco a poco
blurbEn: One suffix gives you dozens of new words at once: take an adjective you know and add -mente.
body:
Mi profesora habla muy claramente. Repite las cosas lentamente y explica todo tranquilamente, sin prisa.

Al principio yo entendía solamente una palabra de cada diez. Ahora entiendo bastante, aunque todavía leo lentamente.

Ella siempre dice lo mismo: «Estás aprendiendo perfectamente. Simplemente necesitas tiempo».

Probablemente tiene razón. El español no es especialmente difícil, pero tampoco es rápido.

Últimamente estoy estudiando media hora todos los días. No es mucho, pero es exactamente lo que ella recomienda.
translationEn:
My teacher speaks very clearly. She repeats things slowly and explains everything calmly, without hurrying.

At first I understood only one word in ten. Now I understand quite a lot, although I still read slowly.

She always says the same thing: "You are learning perfectly well. You simply need time."

She is probably right. Spanish is not especially difficult, but it is not fast either.

Lately I have been studying half an hour every day. It is not much, but it is exactly what she recommends.

claramente.note: From the adjective 'claro' you already know. Add -mente and you have the adverb.

lentamente.note: From 'lento'. Note it is the feminine form that takes the ending: lenta + mente.

Últimamente.note: The adjective keeps its accent when -mente is added.

phrases.note: Spanish *has* reason rather than *is* right — like having years and having luck.
